claims.knowledge: Three-phase stator armature, DC rotor field, salient versus cylindrical rotors, slip-ring excitation and motor/generator energy direction.
claims.scope: Lecture p. 3. MIT Chapter 9 pp. 1–6, 10–11; NPTEL Section 3.2 supports why a single reactance is insufficient for general saliency. Brushless/PM variants are mentioned only to delimit this wound-field chapter.

claims.knowledge: Synchronous speed, electrical/mechanical angle, equal steady rotor and field speeds; load-angle and generator/motor direction convention.
claims.scope: Lecture pp. 4, 6. MIT Chapter 9 pp. 5–7 and 10. MIT initially uses peak amplitudes and motor current reference; lesson converts to RMS and outgoing generator current.

claims.knowledge: Sinusoidal winding EMF, three-phase displacement, open-circuit equality and saturation of the excitation characteristic.
claims.scope: Lecture p. 4. EMF equation uses RMS per-phase voltage and the conventional rounded coefficient 4.44. Qualitative OCC has no numeric axes or purported measured data.

claims.knowledge: Armature reaction, resultant MMF and linear flux superposition; leakage plus armature-reaction reactance equals synchronous reactance.
claims.scope: Lecture pp. 5, 8. NPTEL Section 3.1 and 3.2. Magnetic superposition requires linearity; a constant-Xs round-rotor model is an approximation.

claims.knowledge: Generator and motor KVL; RMS complex power; current phase and perpendicular jXsI drop; copper loss and conversion power.
claims.scope: Lecture p. 8 uses outgoing current. NPTEL generator equations 24, 32–35 and motor equations 58–61 agree when current directions are reconciled. Three-phase power is three times per-phase power.

claims.knowledge: Lossless round-rotor P and Q equations, current from phasors, excitation and reactive exchange, unity-power-factor condition and torque/power relation.
claims.scope: Explicit extension beyond the supplied nine-page lecture. Derived from the lecture equivalent circuit, checked against MIT pp. 6–10 and NPTEL equation 35. Positive output means exported P/Q; RMS magnitudes replace MIT initial peak phasors.

claims.knowledge: Ideal maximum at 90 electrical degrees; local power-angle slope; salient-pole limitation; calculated P-Q locus is not a thermal capability curve.
claims.scope: MIT Chapter 9 pp. 10–12; NPTEL Section 3.2. These are model limits, not a rated operating-envelope claim or transient assessment.

claims.knowledge: Zero average synchronous torque for a stationary excited rotor; variable-frequency controlled start and damper-cage induction start; ideal cage current disappears at synchronous speed.
claims.scope: Lecture pp. 6–7. NPTEL sections 6.1 and 6.2.1/6.2.3, MIT Chapter 9 p. 10. Starting sequence and timing are schematic; no pull-in transient prediction is claimed.

claims.knowledge: Induction/synchronous comparison; DC versus slip-frequency rotor current; zero real power does not require zero reactive current; consistent voltage and sign conventions.
claims.scope: Summary uses the cited chapter relations; induction comparison is also grounded in Chapter 7 source audit. P=0, Q≠0 is checked directly from the lossless phasor model.

models.title: Synchronous pole-axis animation
models.parameters: f=50 or 60 Hz; total poles=2,4,6,8; electrical delta=−60 to +60 degrees.
models.assumptions: Steady synchronized round-rotor, negligible-resistance interpretation. Common slowdown for both fields. The delta slider selects steady states; no swing equation is solved.
models.checks: Rotor and field have identical animated angular speed for every setting; six-pole 50 Hz speed=1000 rpm.

models.title: Three-phase specified-flux EMF
models.formula: Ephase=4.44 f N Phi kw; Eline=sqrt(3)Ephase for Y; e_k=sqrt(2)Ephase sin(2pi f t+alpha_k).
models.assumptions: Sinusoidal prescribed flux. No field-current-to-flux or saturation model. Fixed voltage axis allows honest amplitude comparison.
models.checks: Example gives Ephase=506.16 V, Eline=876.69483676 V; three instantaneous phase voltages sum to zero analytically.

models.title: Head-to-tail generator phasor
models.formula: I=Iabs exp(j phi); Ef=V+(Ra+jXs)I; Sout=3V conj(I); Pcu=3I²Ra.
models.parameters: V=230 V/phase; Ra=.20 ohm; Xs=2 ohm; I=0–50 A; outgoing current angle=−75 to +75 degrees.
models.assumptions: RMS phase quantities, balanced steady-state, illustrative fixed parameters. Current arrow uses direction-only scale and is labeled accordingly.
models.checks: At 30 A and 0.8 lagging: I=24−j18 A, Ef=270.8+j44.4 V, P=16560 W, Q=12420 var, copper loss=540 W.

models.title: Power-angle and P-Q locus
models.formula: I=(Ef exp(j delta)−V)/(jXs); P=3VEf sin(delta)/Xs; Q=3V(Ef cos(delta)−V)/Xs.
models.parameters: V=230 V/phase, Xs=2 ohm, Ra=0; Ef=160–360 V/phase, delta=−85 to +85 degrees.
models.assumptions: Lossless cylindrical rotor; ideal stiff bus; illustrative parameters; saliency, saturation, thermal, protection and transient limits omitted. P-Q arc is a model locus, not a capability rating.
models.checks: 385 E/delta points checked: S magnitude=3V|I|; P(−delta)=−P(delta); Q(−delta)=Q(delta). At E=V and delta=0, I=0 and PF undefined. At E=280 V, delta=0: P=0, Q=17250 var.

models.title: Conceptual starting sequence
models.formula: Stationary synchronous torque normalized as sin(relative electrical angle). VFD uses prescribed n=ns ramp; cage start prescribes n/ns increasing before capture.
models.parameters: Display ramp 10 s, illustrative cage progression 9 s; displayed durations are animation timing only.
models.assumptions: Not a mechanical dynamic model or a real starting-time prediction. No inertia, load torque, current regulator, excitation transient or pull-in calculation.
models.checks: Fixed-rotor torque integrates to zero over 2pi; VFD view maintains equal rotor and field speeds; cage field/slip distinction is shown and changes at conceptual capture.

examples.given: Pout=20 kW; Qout=0; V=230 V/phase; Xs=2 ohm; Ra=0.

errata: The supplied synchronous lecture contains no worked numeric examples. All three added examples are explicitly labeled derived teaching examples with selected values.

MIT Chapter 9 begins with peak-amplitude phasors and a motor current reference. The lesson uses RMS phase magnitudes and outgoing generator current, hence factors of 3 rather than 3/2 and reversed power signs.

MIT Chapter 9 p. 10 per-unit reactive-power line appears to contain sin(delta); its earlier derived reactive-power equation uses cos(delta). The cosine form is independently obtained from 3VI* and used here.
NPTEL Section 3 equation 24 is displayed with an omitted I in one preceding typeset line; the explicit V=Et−IZs equation and diagram establish the intended KVL. The full complex product is used here.
The qualitative open-circuit characteristic has no claimed numeric calibration. Starting ramps/capture are conceptual, not fabricated measured trajectories.

The primary starting notes describe a torque reversal each half cycle. This chapter states the unambiguous sinusoidal torque and zero cycle average without treating the reversal count as a doubled sinusoidal frequency.

All circuits, rotor sketches, inverter symbol and plotted data are original explanatory renderings driven by cited relationships. No copied figure, unverified machine performance data or purported experimental video is included.
